s: A Parma gelato lab built on the founder's refusal motto — 'gelato, nothing else' — tucked in the small square behind Piazza Garibaldi.
w: Ciacco was founded by Stefano Guizzetti in Parma; the name and 'senz'altro' ('nothing else') tagline signal a house rule against artificial flavourings, colourants and industrial bases. The brand later opened a second shop on Via Spadari in central Milan. Alongside gelato, the Parma shop is known for a handmade colomba/panettone-style cake in season.
_facts: Piazza della Steccata 1A, 43121 Parma
Founded by Stefano Guizzetti
Second shop at Via Spadari 13, Milan

s: A gelato-and-chocolate lab in Fidenza's centre named for Magritte, run by two makers who source from small local farms.
w: Magritte - Gelati al Cubo is the project of Gian Luca (Cavi) and Giulia, with shops in Fidenza and Piacenza, Emilia-Romagna. Gambero Rosso has named it among Italy's best gelaterias for four consecutive years, and Gianluca Cavi separately received the guide's 'Gelatiere Emergente' recognition. The lab also makes its own chocolate.
_facts: Via Cavour 72, 43036 Fidenza (PR)
Second shop: Via IV Novembre 152, Piacenza
Named among Gambero Rosso's best Italian gelaterias for 4 consecutive years

s: A fully gluten-free gelato shop in Turin's San Salvario quarter that doubles as a tiny natural-wine and pantry store.
w: Papalele is the gluten-free gelateria project of Emanuele Monero, with two shops in Turin — one in San Salvario, one at Porta Palazzo. Every flavour, cone and cake is made without gluten, and there's a wide vegan range made without eggs. Flavours push past the classics into pairings like raspberry-hibiscus-kombucha sorbet and a savoury miso-and-sesame scoop.
_facts: Corso Guglielmo Marconi 23/A, 10125 Turin (San Salvario)
Founder Emanuele Monero; entirely gluten-free menu
Ranked #2 in Italy by the Dissapore 2025 gelateria guide

s: A family-run Trapani gelateria on the seafront viale, repeatedly ranked among the very best in Italy for its restrained, additive-free recipes.
w: Gelateria Liparoti is a family gelato business with its flagship on Trapani's Viale delle Sirene and a second shop up the hill in Erice. It placed first at the Grand Prix Gelato Italia 2023 and was named the 5th-best gelateria in Italy for 2026 by Dissapore (first in Sicily). Besides Sicilian staples like pistachio, the shop is known for pairings such as chocolate with chili pepper.
_facts: Viale delle Sirene 21, 91100 Trapani
Second shop: Via Vittorio Emanuele 86, Erice
1st place, Grand Prix Gelato Italia 2023

s: A no-additives gelateria chain in Brianza built on Slow Food, zero-km and organic sourcing, with an outpost as far afield as Brooklyn.
w: L'Albero dei Gelati operates out of the Brianza area northeast of Milan, with locations in Monza, Seregno and Cogliate (plus a Park Slope, Brooklyn branch). It makes gelato without preservatives, colourants or artificial flavourings, using organic butter and milk from Valtellina, zero-km eggs, and seasonal organic fruit used only when ripe.
_facts: Via Giuseppe Sirtori 1, 20900 Monza (MB)
Sister shops in Seregno and Cogliate; US outpost in Park Slope, Brooklyn
Listed in Dissapore's 2026 ranking of Italy's 100 best artisanal gelaterias

s: A historic Reggio Emilia gelateria reinvented by a former IT professional into one of Emilia-Romagna's most decorated gelato labs.
w: In 2010, Simone De Feo left an IT career to take over the historic Capolinea gelateria on Reggio Emilia's Viale Simonazzi, and it has held Gambero Rosso's 'Tre Coni' award every year since 2017. The lab works seasonally and excludes semi-processed ingredients, synthetic aromas, emulsifiers and hydrogenated fats — flavours range from zabaione and pistachio to robiola with sour cherries and rosemary.
_facts: Viale Ettore Simonazzi 14, 42121 Reggio Emilia
Master gelatiere Simone De Feo took over the site in 2010
Gambero Rosso 'Tre Coni' award holder every year since 2017

s: A neighbourhood gelateria south of Parma's centre that treats flavour combinations like small experiments, not a menu.
w: Al Polo ("gelato pensato") is a small artisan shop on Via La Spezia known for a large vegan gelato selection alongside its classic recipes. In 2025 it placed 13th in Dissapore's ranking of Italy's 100 best artisan gelaterie, and it won the World Best Tiramisù award in 2026.
_facts: Via La Spezia 14/A, 43125 Parma
Ranked 13th of Italy's 100 best gelaterie by Dissapore in 2025
Won World Best Tiramisù 2026

s: A small fair-trade gelateria steps from Piazza Santa Maria in Trastevere, run by a world-champion gelatiere who has been folding organic and fair-trade ingredients into gelato since before it was fashionable.
w: Fiordiluna is the flagship shop of Eugenio Morrone, the Calabria-born gelatiere who won the Gelato World Cup in 2020 and the European gelato championship in 2016. The shop has championed fair-trade ingredients since 1990, when it introduced one of Italy's first 100%-fair-trade gelato flavours, and still serves only in cups, with wafers sold separately.
_facts: Via della Lungaretta 96, Trastevere, Rome
Owner Eugenio Morrone won the Gelato World Cup 2020 and European gelato title 2016
Fair-trade sourcing since 1990

s: Florence's oldest artisan gelateria, a few steps from Santa Croce, still churning gelato the family way since 1930.
w: Vivoli has operated near Santa Croce since 1930 and is widely credited as one of the shops that defined modern Florentine gelato-making, still using traditional batch freezers rather than pre-made bases. It is famous for its affogato, and in 2025 the family leased the adjoining unit to open a dedicated Affogato Bar next door.
_facts: Via dell'Isola delle Stinche 7R, Florence
Operating since 1930, one of Florence's oldest gelaterie
Opened a dedicated Affogato Bar next door in 2025

s: A pocket-sized family gelateria tucked into a pedestrian calle in Castello, well off the San Marco tourist churn.
w: Gallonetto has served artisanal gelato from this Castello address since 1985; after a hiatus, the family shop was reopened in 2021 by Sara and Thomas, who kept the original recipes and sourcing — Piedmont hazelnuts, organic lemons, fresh mascarpone — across roughly 30 rotating flavours.
_facts: Salizada San Lio 5727, Castello, Venice
Family shop dating to 1985, reopened under second generation in 2021
Open daily 10:30-23:00

s: A science-minded gelateria steps from Playa de la Victoria, run by an industrial chemist who traded lab work for gelato.
w: Carlo Guerriero, a Venetian gelatiere with degrees in industrial chemistry and environmental science, opened La Cremería near Playa de la Victoria in April 2011. In 2024 it was ranked 7th in the world by the Gelato Festival World Ranking, one of only two Spanish shops ever to crack the global top ten.
_facts: Avenida Periodista Beatriz Cienfuegos 6, Cádiz
Opened April 2011, near Playa de la Victoria
Ranked 7th in the world, Gelato Festival World Ranking 2024

s: A small-town ice cream house in rural Opolskie that has quietly become a fixture of Poland's competitive gelato circuit.
w: The Szypuła family has made ice cream at this Baborów address since 1974, when founder Stanisław Szypuła began selling from a market-square window; his son Tomasz now runs the shop, café and confectionery as Lodziarnia Pod Orzechem ('Ice Cream House Under the Walnut Tree'). Tomasz was crowned Master of the Polish Ice Cream Industry at the 2017 EXPO SWEET championships and placed 8th worldwide in the Gelato Festival World Ranking.
_facts: ul. Moniuszki 5, Baborów, Opole Voivodeship
Business founded 1974 by Stanisław Szypuła, now run by son Tomasz
Tomasz Szypuła: Polish Ice Cream Champion 2017, ranked 8th in Gelato Festival World Ranking

s: A suburban pastry counter on a District XVI arterial road where a self-taught farm-town confectioner makes the gelato that beat the rest of the planet.
w: Founded as a family confectionery in the village of Kisnémedi and later run from Rétság, Fazekas Cukrászda now supplies its Budapest counter on Csömöri út from that same countryside kitchen. Ádám Fazekas, the family's gelato maker, topped the Gelato Festival World Ranking in 2024 (227 points, three crowns) and was inducted into the Gelato Festival Hall of Fame in Rome in May 2026.
_facts: Csömöri út 209, 1162 Budapest (16th district)
Ádám Fazekas ranked #1 on the Gelato Festival World Ranking 2024
Inducted into the Gelato Festival Hall of Fame, Rome, May 2026

s: A seafront-square gelateria on the Riviera di Ponente run by a judge of the Gelato World Masters, a short walk from the Varazze promenade.
w: Opened in 2001 on Varazze's central square facing the seafront, I Giardini di Marzo is run by Marco Venturino, who was named the world's best gelato maker in the 2022 Gelato Festival World Ranking. The house signature is 'Liguretto,' a trademarked sorbetto built from Ligurian lemons and Genoese PDO basil.
_facts: Piazza Dante Alighieri 28, Varazze (SV)
Marco Venturino ranked #1 in the Gelato Festival World Ranking 2022
Signature trademarked flavor 'Liguretto': Ligurian lemon and Genoese basil DOP

s: A Sardinian gelato counter steps from La Jolla Cove, its patio looking straight out over the water.
w: Opened in February 2013 by Sardinian native Andrea Racca with longtime friend Marco Saba, Bobboi takes its name from the Sardinian dialect word for 'delicious small sweet.' Gelato maker Monica Maccioni, trained at the Università del Gelato in Bologna, blends California ingredients into traditional Italian technique across roughly eighteen rotating flavors.
_facts: 8008 Girard Ave, La Jolla, San Diego, CA 92037
Founded February 2013 by Andrea Racca and Marco Saba
Outdoor patio has a direct view of La Jolla Cove

s: A century-old Sicilian ice-cream-and-pastry parlor in Mid-City that came back from five feet of Katrina floodwater to reopen within a year.
w: Angelo Brocato, born in Cefalù, Sicily, opened his New Orleans shop in 1905 in the French Quarter, moving to a larger Ursulines Street parlor in 1921 modeled on Palermo's ice cream halls. The business relocated to its present Mid-City building in 1978. Hurricane Katrina's floodwaters submerged the shop under roughly five feet of water in 2005, but it reopened in September 2006. Signature items include spumoni, cannoli siciliana, and biscuit tortoni.
_facts: 214 N Carrollton Ave, New Orleans, LA 70119
Founded 1905 by Sicilian immigrant Angelo Brocato; moved to present Mid-City location in 1978
Flooded ~5 feet during Hurricane Katrina; reopened September 2006
